The romance of chivalry fascinates many people. Courageous, armoured
knights clash in a whirl of heraldic splendour; beautiful, eloquent ladies
bestow their embroidered sleeves and favors; squires dash hither and fro,
lightly armoured, helping their knights as they may. 

The spectacle and color of the medieval tournament draws us towards
the very heart our Western tradition. During the 12th - 16th centuries,
the medieval tournament was a primary vehicle for bringing an ideal to
life. Prowess, courage & loyalty--the warrior virtues--were wedded
for a brief time to the civilizing virtues advocated by church and court.
These ideals, written by poets, churchmen, and even some of the knights
themselves, still stand today is testimony to the high ideals to which
man might aspire. 

Today there are thousands of gentle men and women who find an interest
in these images, images whose power is realized by students, re-enactors,
and by people who find something missing in our "ethicless" societies.

There are many re-enactment groups now participating in the reconstruction
of medieval tournaments. These events range widely in their authenticity
and their focuses, but share a common interest in the history and romance
of an idea that has never completely died. These groups range in size from
ten to thirty thousand; from the small bands who form tournament companies
to the largest of the tournament societies, the

Society for Creative Anachronism (SCA).
 

Alongside these groups stand a few scholars, collectors, craftsmen and
spectators who study, read, create beautiful reproductions, or simply attend
the Renaissance Faires. A quantity of high quality resources are available
to the tournament re-enactor, and it is a goal of 
Chronique,

Journal of Chivalry
 to bring these resources together so that the
experiences of these medieval tournament reconstructions can be as accurate,
and as powerful as possible. 

It is the intent of the editors to offer this WWW page as a resource
base, a place where those interested in medieval tournametns can share
and exchange information. We will continue to offer new pointers and resources
as they become available, and would like to encourage those interested
in these reconstructions to subscribe to the print journal. 

Note that this homepage is under construction--please let us know what
you like and what doesn't seem to work right!
